main_text.p: Quocirca ut partis similaris sanitatem, ita & morbum necesse est in tribus constitui, triaq; fieri similarium morborum genera, unum materię, alterum temperamenti, ter-tium totius substantiæ. Hæc Fernelius: ad quorum singula nos quoq; respondere ex-pedit. Quod in primis ait, similaris partis nostri corporis sanitate esse integritatem & moderationem materiæ, formæ, & tem-peramenti, nullis ambagibus inuolutū uidetur? Nam materiæ integritas nihil est a-liud quā forma, quæ illa perficit, & ei essen-tiam tribuit. Etenim materia sine forma & integritate est duntaxat ens potentia, quæ nec quid est, nec quale, neq; quantū, quem-admodum septimo Sapientię libro nos do-cet philosophus. Proinde integritatem ma-teriæ esse similaris partis sanitatem frustra profert Fernelius. Deinde integritatem for-mæ esse similaris partis sanitatem non minus insulse dixit. Quasi uero quędam fit for-ma essentialis corporis alicuius imperfe-cta, cū ea sit corporis physici natura & per-fectio. Præterea materia & forma, quòd substantiæ sint, nec intendi, neque remitti queunt. Idcirco ipsis moderatio perperam tribuitur. Quapropter partis similaris sani-tas

page.notes: Catchword "tas" and signature "E 5" are printed at the foot. Line 1 "Quocirca" starts mid-sentence, so the paragraph is marked as a continuation from the previous page. The printed "feftio" in line 24 is read as "fectio" (ct ligature). The printed "cū" in line 23 is read as a macron over u. Right-margin „ marks are printer's signs, not text, and are not transcribed. Faint show-through in the right margin is excluded.
